context:
Web research, read-only. Prices and limits marked third-party are unconfirmed.
- PriceCharting: an official paid API gives current prices by TCGplayer id, including PSA 10 and Japanese/Chinese raw. About $49 a month (third-party figure). Whether it gives price history is unconfirmed.
- PSA: a public lookup by cert number, with a daily quota that sources disagree on. Population by set needs scraping. Card Ladder already gives you population, so PSA adds little.
- eBay: sold-item data needs eBay's approval, which may never come. Other routes show live listings only, or your own sales.
home: a new decision record (slug), by a records lane

options.gain: Fills the blank PSA 10 and Japanese/Chinese price fields the slabs screen promises.
options.how: Wire its paid API by TCGplayer id once TCGCSV lands.
options.label: PriceCharting for slabs and Japanese cards
options.lose: A paid subscription. History is unconfirmed.

options.how: Read population by cert from PSA or GemRate.
options.label: PSA population
options.lose: Low value, since Card Ladder already has it. Quota unclear.

options.label: Nothing yet
options.lose: PSA 10 and Japanese price fields stay blank.

ref: spec my-slabs section 4.6 (PSA 10 and Japanese/Chinese prices), DEBT72 (no eBay work without a decision)
title: After TCGCSV, which of PriceCharting, PSA or eBay is worth wiring?
why: It is the only one that fills a field already on screen, through an official API.
